newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT, CRICKET - Fitness key to Doull's success.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT, CRICKET - Fitness key to Doull's success.

text.p: DUNEDIN, March 10 - Simon Doull has found the magical elixir which spells the difference between pleasure and pain for him on the cricket field.
For Doull, fitness equates to form, and he is relishing the fact that his body -- which has so often let him down in the past -- is holding up under the strain of regular work.

The New Zealand fast-medium bowler has been in excellent form this summer, a trend he continued yesterday when picking up his third five-wicket bag in six tests this season to provide the cut and thrust to help dismiss Sri Lanka for 222 in their first innings of the first cricket test at Carisbrook here.

Sri Lanka were 37 without loss in their second innings by stumps on the third day when they still needed high-powered binoculars to sight a distant target of 327 required to make the home side bat again.

After Doull and Heath Davis, who claimed three for 34, combined to dismantle Sri Lanka's initial response, Kiwi captain Stephen Fleming understandably showed no hesitation in enforcing the follow on -- the first time a New Zealand skipper has done so since John Wright led the side to victory over India in Christchurch in 1990.
For Doull, 27, the mystical ingredient which separates success from failure is simple. He's fit.
Plagued by injuries throughout his international career since first appearing for New Zealand in 1992, the Northern Districts seam bowler is relishing having a healthy body.

"This is the first time in five years that I've been able to still play at this time of the season," said Doull, whose five for 58 from 21.2 overs saw him repeat earlier similarly profitable stints in tests this season against Pakistan in Lahore and England in Wellington.
"It is just nice to be playing at this time of the season instead of sitting back on the couch watching.
"I think having the game off in Wellington (the final one-dayer against England last Tuesday) was good for me. It enabled me to have a bit of a rest.
"I came into this game a little fresher than I could have, and maybe that's paid off a little bit."

Doull is not the only bowler to show his credentials in a match which to date has been dominated by the monumental innings of Kiwi opener Bryan Young, whose magnificent 267 not out provided the backbone to his team's imposing first innings total
of 586 for seven declared.
Davis, too, performed with distinction, his figures from 19 overs again illustrating the bright future he has at this level.
Sri Lanka, although wilting under the ferocity of Young's broad bat, unveiled a potential future star in left arm fast bowler Nuwan Zoysa, an 18-year-old with unlimited potential.
Sri Lankan coach Bruce Yardley was enthusiastic about Zoysa's first experience at test level despite the 1.96 metre teenager returning the unflattering figures of one for 112 from 40 overs.

Zoysa was not helped by having two catches dropped off his bowling, but showed plenty of evidence to suggest more experience and exposure to top level batsmen will see him develop into something special.
"I told him he will sometimes bowl worse than he did but instead finish with six or seven wickets.
"I think he's had a fantastic debut," Yardley said of Zoysa, who only eight months ago was wallowing in the obscurity of schoolboy cricket.
"Bryan Young made more than 200 but Zoysa probably beat him outside offstump 25 times.
"We knew Nuwan was going to be pretty good. He's a very laid back sort of person who just floats around."
Zoysa was the only bowler Yardley exempted from criticism he levelled at his side after they won the toss and sent the home team in to bat last Friday.
"Having won the toss our bowlers didn't bowl well enough, it's as simple as that."
It was not as if Yardley was jumping for joy about his batsmen either after they surrendered meekly into the face of some accurate, persistent pressure applied by the New Zealanders.
"I gave a couple of our batsmen a rocket because it looked as if they would have preferred to be somewhere else."
